reasons: Classification is sound: the clause binds our party (IBM/Customer) one-way and its duration ('[*] years' from the Effective Date, plural 'years') exceeds the 12-month fallback limit, so it fails the fallback on a material term while remaining short of walk-away (no no-hire, scope limited to Transferred Employees, carve-outs for unsolicited contacts, general advertising and search firms).

Redline is directionally correct and minimal: only the duration is changed to twelve (12) months, leaving the already-acceptable scope and carve-outs intact, exactly as the redline guidance directs (changed-character ratio 0.30 is confined to the period term).

Failed deterministic check on 'general-solicitation carve-out present' is a phrasing artifact — the clause does contain a general-advertising/independent-search-firm carve-out ('by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto'), so this is not a substantive defect.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it states what changed (12-month cap), why (multi-year term exceeds policy), confirms the scope/carve-outs are acceptable, and offers a negotiation landing zone.

Minor, non-disqualifying notes: the 18-month landing zone offered is looser than the playbook's 12-month fallback (though still well inside the >24-month walk-away line), and the absence of a reciprocal covenant on MSL is correctly noted as non-burdensome to us rather than flagged.
